climbing_route.label: Upper north ridge above 5,200 ft
climbing_route.notes: The ridge opens into rockier, more open terrain. Snow patches linger later in the season and are more persistent on the east side of the crest than on the drier, rockier crest itself. On a dry ridge the whole route stays class 3-4 scrambling with no roped climbing required; an ice axe and light traction (microspikes/crampons) are worth carrying in early-to-mid season.

climbing_route.label: Cliff band bypass at ~5,400 ft (crux)
climbing_route.notes: The ridge runs into a cliff band directly below the summit. Do not attempt the band head-on — veer left (east) off the crest into a small gully and take a rising traverse into the upper summit basin. Helmet warranted for rockfall off the cliff band.

climbing_route.label: Final snow to the 6,259 ft summit
climbing_route.notes: The last ~20 vertical feet cross steep snow and a few small trees. Ice axe and light traction are worth having for this final snow pitch.

climbing_route.label: Southwest snowfields
climbing_route.notes: From the base of the southwest face, climb steepening southwest-facing snowfields toward the distinctive 'cowskull-shaped' snowfield high on the face — the key navigational landmark, described as looking like a ghost early season. Start early: afternoon softening and thunderstorm exposure are the concern.

climbing_route.label: Snow chute and the cowskull
climbing_route.notes: Ascend a snow chute and then the cowskull snowfield itself, where the angle steepens enough that many parties place running-belay pickets.

climbing_route.label: Loose scree to the summit ridge
climbing_route.notes: Above the snow, step off, remove crampons, and grovel up loose scree and rubble to gain the summit ridge.

climbing_route.label: Summit ridge
climbing_route.notes: About 100 ft of class 2-3 rock scrambling along the ridge to the true summit.

climbing_route.label: Druid Plateau to the base of the summit block
climbing_route.notes: From just below 8,000 ft turn northwest and climb steep talus/scree — snow-covered into mid-summer — onto the Druid Plateau (~8,350 ft), where Cannon's summit block comes into view. Cross the plateau and take the western slopes to the base of the block. Serious route-finding terrain: no cairns and no tread, snow frequently holding into July, exposed to sun and lightning with no bail-out shelter.

climbing_route.label: Summit block friction slab
climbing_route.notes: The final ~15 ft to the true summit is a low-angle but exposed friction slab, climbed via a ramp on the block's south side with almost no positive holds. Approach shoes with good rubber, or rock shoes, make a real difference.

climbing_route.label: Traverse above the tarn
climbing_route.notes: From high camp on the snowy saddle (~5,100 ft), traverse above Anderson/Valkyrie Lake, which is often still frozen.

climbing_route.label: Snow finger to Flypaper Pass (~6,500 ft)
climbing_route.notes: Climb the steep snow finger to the pass. Glacier recession has steepened it considerably beyond older guidebook descriptions, with the crux section now estimated at 40+ degrees late in the season. Plan to be through it before it melts out — ideally spring or early summer — and expect firm or icy snow requiring an ice axe and crampons. Carry water from the tarn near high camp; there is none above.

climbing_route.label: Talus gully above the avalanche bench
climbing_route.notes: From the broad, flat bench of avalanche debris about 200 ft above Buckhorn Lake — the true start of the off-trail scramble — climb a wide talus/scree gully trending south then curving east, breaking treeline around 5,800 ft (roughly 700 ft above the lake), where the going turns to loose rock and light class 2-3 scrambling. Avalanche debris and blowdown near the lake.

climbing_route.label: Loose slopes to the Iron-Worthington col (~6,420 ft)
climbing_route.notes: Angle east/southeast up increasingly loose slopes to the col. Sustained loose scree and talus underfoot — helmet recommended for rockfall from parties above. Route-finding on a faint, unmarked path with sparse cairns; a GPS track or Mountaineers/SummitPost beta is strongly advised.

climbing_route.label: Summit fin
climbing_route.notes: From the col, angle northeast up open slopes to the base of Worthington's summit fin. The final class 3 scramble drops a few feet left of the ridge crest to a short (~10 ft) crack, then follows the top of the fin to the true summit.

climbing_route.label: Summit block from the basin
climbing_route.notes: From the Kindy Ridge / Cyclone Lake basin, reach Mutchler's summit block by heather and blocky rock slopes rising out of the basin — moderate class 2-3 scrambling, with some loose rock near the top.
